name: Value Proposition Canvas
description:
A value proposition articulates why a particular group might find a product, service or intervention valuable. It connects the circumstances, needs or goals of that group with the benefits a proposed offering intends to create.

Developing a value proposition can help teams make assumptions explicit and examine whether a concept addresses something people actually value.
whenToUse: Use value proposition work when developing or refining a concept and when the relationship between the proposed offering and the needs it addresses remains unclear.
steps: Define the group or situation being addressed.
Identify relevant goals, needs and difficulties from research.
Describe the proposed product or service.
Explain what benefit it intends to create.
State why the proposition might be meaningfully different.
Test the proposition through research and prototypes.
Revise the statement as evidence develops.
lookOutFor: A value proposition is a hypothesis until supported by evidence.
Avoid inventing customer needs simply to justify an existing solution.
Value may be social, public, environmental or experiential as well as commercial.

resources.citation: Osterwalder, A. et al. (2014). *Value Proposition Design*. Wiley.
